children: Tamarack Valley Energy agreed to merge with Headwater Exploration in an all-stock deal that the companies say would create Canada's largest pure-play oil producer focused on the Clearwater Formation.

Under the deal, valued at 10 billion Canadian dollars, equivalent to US$7.24 billion, Headwater shareholders will receive one Tamarack common share per each Headwater share held, the companies said Tuesday. Tamarack will issue 237.8 million common to acquire all of Headwater's issued and outstanding common shares.
Tamarack shareholders will own 66.5% of the combined entity, which will be led by Tamarack's current management team. Headwater shareholders will own the remaining stake.
The companies said the deal would offer a "differentiated value proposition from the enhanced efficiency, profitability and durability of a combined Clearwater asset base."

The deal is expected to be immediately accretive to Tamarack's free funds flow per share and enhance its five-year plan, positioning the combined company to deliver higher total shareholder returns, they said.
Certain noncore exploration assets will be transferred to a new exploration company, Tributary Exploration, which will be led by Headwater's current management team, the companies said.

Tamarack expects its 2026 capital program to range from C$450 million to C$470 million, reflecting incremental spending associated with Headwater's planned capital program and subject to the deal's completion.
The companies' combined capital investment programs for the year are expected to total about C$700 million.
The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter.
